conflict_topics: wheelchair access / tent blocking lift access
evening prayers/wake noise vs. night-shift sleep schedule
occupation of void deck vs. morning exercise group
dialogue_quality_notes: Tone is polite and neighbourly; participants offer condolences before raising needs, e.g., 'my condolences' followed by a request.
Concrete proposals reduce conflict: 'What about the other side of the block? The space near the other lift lobby.' and 'Maybe if they are pointed away from the block, it could help.'
Agent D is responsive but sometimes defers (e.g., 'my head isn't really in the right space to think about it right now'), which slowed solution-finding for some issues.
A minor amount of repeated thanking occurs (Rounds 10–11) but no substantive repetition of unresolved positions.
evaluation.final_reason: Two substantive issues were affirmatively settled in the conversation while one remained unresolved. Morning exercise: Agent A proposed an alternative sheltered spot and Agent C accepted it ('What about the other side of the block?...' / 'that space should work.'), so the morning-use conflict was clarified and accommodated. Evening-noise: Agent B requested quieter/redirected sound and suggested pointing speakers away; Agent D agreed: 'We can do that. I'll make sure they point away from the block.' Both sides voiced concrete mutual acceptance, so the noise mitigation was agreed in round 10. Wheelchair access: Agent A raised that the tent blocked wheelchair access and Agent D said 'let me get my uncle, we'll shift things,' but there is no later confirmation that the tent was actually moved; that incompatibility remained unsettled at the transcript end.
position_change_notes: Agent C changed position on the morning-space conflict by accepting Agent A's alternative: 'that space should work.'
Agent D shifted from a general commitment to be mindful about noise to accepting a concrete technical mitigation: 'I'll make sure they point away from the block.'

Agent A and Agent B remained consistent: A advocated for wheelchair access and proposed an alternate space for C's group; B consistently sought quiet during his sleep window and proposed speaker-direction as a solution.
The wheelchair-access issue remained contested: Agent D expressed intent to move things ('we'll shift things') but did not confirm completion; Agent A's need remained unrelieved in the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A raises a practical incompatibility: '...looking at the tent... I don't think my mother's wheelchair can get through to the lift.' Agent D offers to move things but no confirmed action: 'let me get my uncle, we'll shift things. Can you show us how much space you need...?' (problem stated; willingness to act but no settlement).

A second substantive incompatibility appears: Agent B says he must sleep in the evenings due to night shift: 'my bedroom is right above here, and I'm on the night shift this week. I have to sleep in the evenings before I go to work.' No mitigation yet from Agent D in this round.

Positions are explicitly incompatible on timing: Agent D: 'The evening prayers are an important part of the wake... We will be sure to finish by 10:30 each night.' Agent B: 'I understand, but that's actually the whole time I need to sleep... From about 6 p.m. to 10:30.' This makes the collision strong (overlapping essential needs).

A new substantive conflict about morning use arises: Agent C: '...we meet here at 7 a.m. every day.' Agent D: '...the wake will be going on throughout the day. The space will be occupied in the mornings as well.' Multiple incompatible uses (wheelchair access, night sleep, morning exercise) remain unresolved.

Agent C asks for alternate sheltered space for morning group: 'The other open space is by the playground, but there's no shade... Is there any other sheltered space around here we could use for an hour in the mornings?' Agent D declines to consider solutions this round: 'I wouldn't know. My head isn't really in the right space to think about it right now.' Conflict over morning use persists without resolution.

Agents begin proposing solutions: Agent C asks others for ideas; Agent A proposes alternative sheltered spot: 'What about the other side of the block? The space near the other lift lobby. It's also sheltered.' This reduces the morning-use conflict though it's not yet accepted by C in this round.

Agent C accepts the proposed alternative: 'Ah, that's a good idea, Agent A. ... that space should work.' Morning-exercise conflict is effectively settled, but the wheelchair-access and night-noise conflicts remain.

Agent B requests quieter singing: 'Would it be possible to maybe keep the singing a little softer?...' Agent D responds with a tentative mitigation: 'I will speak to my family. We'll do our best to be mindful of the noise.' Voluntary mitigation reduces tension but does not fully settle the sleep/noise incompatibility.

Agent B clarifies which nights are problematic and suggests a concrete mitigation: 'Are you using speakers? Maybe if they are pointed away from the block, it could help.' At this point D has not yet accepted the specific suggestion within the round.

Agent D accepts the concrete mitigation: 'That's a good idea. We can do that. I'll make sure they point away from the block.' Agent B replies: 'That should help a lot.' The noise-direction arrangement is mutually agreed (speech-only concrete agreement), reducing the unresolved conflict to the wheelchair-access issue only.
Only polite acknowledgment occurs: Agent B repeats thanks; Agent D replies. No new substantive movement on the remaining wheelchair-access issue (still no confirmed repositioning recorded).

No public speech or observable action recorded. Outstanding substantive conflict (wheelchair access past the tent) remains unresolved because the promised shifting of things was not confirmed in the transcript.

substantive_insights: There are three distinct kinds of incompatibility: a physical-access problem (tent blocking wheelchair path), a temporal/noise problem (wake/prayers overlapping a neighbour's sleep window), and a competing-use problem (morning exercise needing sheltered space).

Concrete, actionable proposals (alternate location; redirecting speakers) allowed rapid settlements for two issues; vaguer commitments (promise to 'shift things' without confirmation) left the physical-access problem unresolved.
Permitted use of the void deck (Agent D's family has a permit) mattered less conversationally than neighbors' practical needs; negotiation focused on mitigations rather than on revoking the permit.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 10 because the final status is partially_resolved.
